fingerprint.method: librosa 1.0.0 on the supplied 44.1 kHz/16-bit stereo WAV (decoded from a 128 kbps source per the filename), analysed mono at 22,050 Hz; ffmpeg ebur128 for loudness. No human or model listening took place: every row below is a signal statistic or an attributed description.
fingerprint.tempo: 103 BPM. Beat tracker 103.4; frame-wise tempogram mode 103 (4,480 frames vs 815 for the runner-up 123). Shazam also lists 103 BPM. Half/double-time readings (51.5 / 206) are not supported by the tempogram.
fingerprint.key: Unresolved between two readings. Krumhansl–Schmuckler on mean chroma ranks C♯ minor (r = 0.71) ahead of C♯ major (0.62); chroma peaks are G♯, C♯, A, F♯, E. A community chord chart (Ultimate Guitar, user noah.paxman53, standard tuning, no capo) gives a D–F♯m–A–E loop, which is diatonic to A major / F♯ minor. The chart's D chord is weak in the chroma (0.35), so the recording's tonal centre should be confirmed by ear before it is quoted.
fingerprint.loudness: Integrated −7.4 LUFS, loudness range 5.2 LU, true peak +0.2 dBTP: a loud, compressed modern pop master, not a quiet acoustic recording.
fingerprint.texture: Percussive-to-harmonic energy ratio stays low (0.23–0.32) and onset density falls from ~2/s in the first minute to 0.2–0.4/s after 1:20. The signal is sustained-chord and vocal dominated rather than drum-forward; sharp transients are sparse once the full arrangement is in.
fingerprint.stereo: Left/right correlation 0.53 — a moderately wide mix.
fingerprint.lyrics: Not reproduced. Perspective per the Shazam lyric page and the community chord chart: first-person verses about restlessness, time passing and friends moving on; a second-person pre-chorus about getting lost in the dark on the way to someone's heart; verse 2 and the bridge turn to Jesus/Christ 'turning the lights back on' and an invitation into the light. The chorus repeats the title line eight times; the bridge repeats its own four-word mantra and interlocks with the final chorus. YouTube tags added by the channel include 'jesus turned the lights back on'.
fingerprint.arrangement_source: Section labels below align the chord chart's structure (intro · verse 1 · pre · chorus · verse 2 · pre · chorus · bridge · chorus 2) with the energy and bass-share boundaries found by agglomerative segmentation at 19.0, 55.9, 74.9, 111.8, 130.8 and 168.7 s. Labels are inferred, not heard.

timeline.label: Intro (inferred)
timeline.obs: −14 dB RMS, almost no low end (bass share ≈1%), bright centroid ≈1.95 kHz. Opens on a single sustained chord per the chart.

timeline.label: Verse 1 + pre-chorus (inferred)
timeline.obs: Level rises to −11 dB; bass share climbs from 2% to 9% by 0:40; onset density drops — sustained strums/pads rather than busy drums.

timeline.label: Chorus 1 entry (inferred)
timeline.obs: Dip to −13.4 dB with the lowest bass share of the song (0.9%) and the brightest centroid (2.1 kHz): the arrangement thins out and lifts up rather than slamming in.

timeline.label: Full chorus / verse 2 (inferred)
timeline.obs: Peak RMS at 1:15; loudest stretch (−9.6 to −10.2 dB) with the fullest low end (bass share 15–17%). Onsets sparse (0.2–0.4/s): weight comes from bass and sustained chords.

timeline.label: Pre-chorus / breakdown (inferred)
timeline.obs: Drops to −12.7 then −14.2 dB; bass share back to 3–8%.

timeline.label: Bridge + final chorus (inferred)
timeline.obs: Returns to −10 dB with 6–11% bass share; the chart's bridge mantra interlocks with the title line here.

timeline.label: Outro
timeline.obs: −20 to −23 dB; percussive ratio falls to 0.10–0.12 — percussion drops out and the song exhales rather than ending on a hit.

attributed_sound: Qobuz/AllMusic bio: a 'minimalist pop duo from the California coast' whose sound 'draws on Frank Ocean'.
Spotify About (band-written): music 'built on faith, friendship, and the pursuit of light in a dark world'.

Vocal delivery and timbre: not assessable from signal statistics — marked Unassessed in every comparison below.

next_steps.step: Run the ear test on the fifteen
next_steps.detail: Listen to the sequence in order with the four-dimension rubric open and overwrite the 'Not heard' cells. Two decisions need ears, not data: the seed's key reading (A major family per chart vs C♯ minor per algorithm) and whether the Oceanside guitar bands actually sit near a minimalist pop duo or only near its audience.

next_steps.step: Watch the Near Kingdom / Oceanside cluster as a scene
next_steps.detail: Three Near Kingdom-curated lists and one label roster account for most of the verified adjacency. Re-pull Christian Pop Hits 2026, Christian Indie Hits and Upbeat Christian songs monthly, log who lands next to the seed, and track new Hopeful., Living Again and Beach Chapel releases as they arrive.

next_steps.step: Build the secular watchlist from the curators, not the charts
next_steps.detail: MOODY INDIE (Landlake music) and SAD VIBES / ALTERNATIVE (@saiyanreece) programmed the seed into secular rooms. Follow those curators' new adds and Chartmetric's similar-artist set (Bennett Coast, Krooked Kings, slenderbodies, Bay Ledges) and re-run co-occurrence after the album cycle, keeping the summer and album versions separate.

limits: No listening. Sonic and vocal judgments are capped at Medium/Unassessed for every candidate, and the seed fingerprint is signal statistics aligned to a community chord chart.

Playlist contents come from Spotify's public embed, which exposes only the first 100 tracks. Any placement beyond #100 (e.g., *JESUS* at #534, granola girl at #266) is resolved but not verified for co-occurrence.
The export has no playlist IDs; identities were resolved by name + curator through Chartmetric (top 12) or Spotify search (small lists). Six names remain unresolved.
Shazam blocked requests after about 25 pages, so BPM/label data covers 10 of 27 accepted recordings.
Chartmetric similar-artist and comparable-track tables were read for page 1 only (Chrome extension disconnected before pagination).
The '28-Day Change' column is a playlist-level Chartmetric field whose exact definition was not verified in-app; it is not song stream growth.
Playlist follower counts are export snapshots and were never summed as an audience figure.
Metrics are dated per platform and never combined across versions; the second Spotify single listing (35dPLCeXcr0ZuRAhOdS0a1) was not merged with the seed.

data_provenance.audio_analysis: librosa 1.0.0 (uv venv, Python 3.12) + ffmpeg ebur128, run 2026-10-20 on the supplied WAV; script outputs retained in session scratchpad (sig.json).
data_provenance.playlist_contents: Spotify public embed JSON (open.spotify.com/embed/playlist/<id>), first 100 tracks; pulled 2026-10-20.
data_provenance.playlist_identity: Chartmetric track → playlists tab (logged-in session) for the top 12 by followers; Spotify search by name for smaller lists; owner confirmed from embed subtitle.
data_provenance.recording_identity: Spotify embed JSON per track (artist URI, release date) and iTunes Search API (Apple ID, genre, release).
data_provenance.similar_songs: Shazam song pages (Apple Music recommendations) read 2026-10-20 before the site blocked further requests.
data_provenance.no_downloads: No candidate audio was downloaded or analysed; no external playlist or account was created; nobody was contacted.
